title: Ray Charles as bandleader and fines for lateness
summary: Full musical freedom, but fines for lateness; anecdote of Ray being late as a sideman.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well did you, when you played with Ray, what was, I mean I know he's kind of a genius himself as far as music goes. How much leeway did he give you?
All the leeway I wanted. All the leeway I wanted.
So you had like control over the band? Yeah. Musically. Did you call out the numbers?
No, he would call out the numbers. The only numbers I would call out was the numbers that we would play as instrumental to him before we would bring him on. Was he pretty hard on the band?

What way? For being late. If you, like see, like in the dance, you're supposed to start at nine o'clock. You had to be there for the half. If you come there one second after 8.30, that's a hundred dollar fine. Uh huh. And uh, one day a guy was late, well somebody was always late. One time a guy was late, and he started raising, saying at this guy uh, for being late. And I started laughing, you know. He said, what you laughing at Wallace? He picked me up and said, why don't you laugh at Wallace? I said, I'll tell you, after you finish tuning the guys out, I said, you remember we used to sing down in New Orleans, and we had to go with Jose Hill Band to play behind Joe Turner, and uh, you were late, and the guys wanted to leave you. Uh huh. And they said, oh that blind so and so, he always late. He always late, coming on the job when he got to spend all our time sitting out there waiting for him. Let's pull off, leave him. I said, oh man, don't leave that guy. I said, poor boy, uh, uh, uh, uh. Blind boy. Yeah. He's here, he doesn't have any relatives here, and uh, he might need that little money to live on for the rest of the week. Nobody always, so while I was talking to him, talking to him, trying to get him to wait a little longer, and Ray came, he was tough, he was knocked, he was loaded. And uh, but when I told him, when I was telling him about it, I said, do you remember that? He said, yeah, but I'm a leader now, I want them to be on time. But he never was on time, when he was a side man. When he was a side man.
